claims.subject: roadmap

claims.normalized_claim: Phase 1 infrastructure calls for a reproducible experiment runner, operator registry and retention sweep tooling.
claims.subject: roadmap

claims.normalized_claim: Phase 2 defines six canonical probe cameras and GOLD metric baselines.
claims.subject: roadmap

claims.normalized_claim: The P0 experiment plan includes depth-provider comparison, MoGe-3 neighbourhoods, primitive fitting, HallPlanner integration, representation budgets and intrinsic decomposition.
claims.subject: roadmap

claims.normalized_claim: The P1 plan groups hall textures, stylized rendering, SWIFT motion and Gaussian splatting into later experiment batches.
claims.subject: roadmap

claims.normalized_claim: The updated roadmap status marks Phases 1, 2, 3 and 3.5 complete and Phase 4 building-reconstruction work in progress.
claims.subject: roadmap

claims.normalized_claim: The roadmap records missing Torch/OpenCV-style ML dependencies as an environment blocker for several model-backed experiments rather than a node-test blocker.

claims.normalized_claim: The post-GOLD benchmark freezes commit 1cb06c4 as its benchmark surface while treating later instrumentation as environment hardening rather than a baseline shift.
claims.subject: benchmark

claims.normalized_claim: MAXIMUM DENNIS is defined as the maximal locally reproducible benchmark with zero Torch, GPU or Modal dependencies.
claims.subject: MAXIMUM-DENNIS

claims.normalized_claim: MAXIMUM DENNIS uses eight deterministic stub providers across DEPTH, GEOMETRY, CLEANUP and COMPLETION stages on five benchmark scenes.
claims.subject: MAXIMUM-DENNIS

claims.normalized_claim: A passing local benchmark is necessary but not sufficient evidence that real ML providers work.
claims.subject: benchmark

claims.normalized_claim: The primary class-regression gate uses expected-classes data with a tolerance of max(40, ten percent of expected), while dorf-marker is required to match exactly.
claims.subject: class-regression

claims.normalized_claim: Tournament provider score is defined as average quality minus runtime in seconds minus memory in hundreds of megabytes.
claims.subject: tournament

claims.normalized_claim: Real providers are classified as environment-blocked in the recorded sandbox because Torch, NumPy, pip and CUDA are unavailable.
claims.subject: providers

claims.normalized_claim: The local benchmark exercises the spatial-kernel benchmark pipeline and does not test the index.html shader path.
claims.subject: benchmark

claims.normalized_claim: All experiment artifacts are intended to be stored content-addressably under artifacts using SHA-256 as the canonical key.
claims.subject: artifacts

claims.normalized_claim: Re-running a deterministic experiment is expected to reproduce bit-identical artifact hashes.
claims.subject: artifacts

claims.normalized_claim: Retention classes are GOLD permanent, PASS 90 days, FAIL 30 days, ERROR 14 days, TEACHER 180 days and REFERENCE permanent.
claims.subject: retention

claims.normalized_claim: Files selected for cleanup are moved to an archive before permanent deletion and receive a grace period.
claims.subject: retention

claims.normalized_claim: An evaluation packet is specified as a self-contained reproducibility bundle containing experiment, environment, git, dependencies, inputs, outputs, results, scripts and logs.
claims.subject: evaluation-packet

claims.normalized_claim: Every artifact is intended to carry a provenance chain including producer, version, seed, git revision, inputs, determinism and metrics.
claims.subject: provenance

claims.normalized_claim: GOLD and REFERENCE artifacts must not be swept even when the artifact store exceeds its configured size budget.
claims.subject: retention

extraction.notes: Technique and hardware-tier claims extracted as UNVERIFIED.

claims.normalized_claim: WonderJourney, WonderWorld, LucidDreamer, Marble and Text2Room are listed as approaches for generating explorable 3D worlds from image or text inputs.
claims.subject: world-generation

claims.normalized_claim: Splatter Image, DreamGaussian, TripoSplat, InfiniSplat, DiffSplat, DiffusionGS and Complete Gaussian Splats are listed as single-image Gaussian-splat generation approaches.
claims.subject: Gaussian-splats

claims.normalized_claim: Feed-forward Gaussian prediction is positioned as especially suitable for weaker hardware because it avoids per-scene optimization.
claims.subject: feed-forward-GS

claims.normalized_claim: The portability proposal keeps one hierarchical 3DGS target format while varying chunk depth and generation technique by hardware tier.
claims.subject: portability

claims.normalized_claim: Bottom-tier generation is proposed around Splatter Image with one chunk level, middle-tier around DreamGaussian and DiffusionGS, and top-tier around Complete Gaussian Splats and Lyra.
claims.subject: hardware-tiers

claims.normalized_claim: The proposed WORLDGEN ablation compares forward-pass splatting against diffusion and occlusion-completion approaches on identical test images.
claims.subject: ablation

extraction.notes: Registry and license-posture claims extracted without verification.

claims.normalized_claim: The style registry states that foreign code is not embedded and that implemented techniques are independently reimplemented from published formulas or concepts.
claims.subject: style-registry

claims.normalized_claim: License class A covers published formulas and classic techniques, class B permissive references used conceptually, class C unclear snippet sources, and class D proprietary or unclear architecture references.
claims.subject: license-classes

claims.normalized_claim: The registry lists sixteen implemented style techniques spanning lighting, specular, rim, normals, outlines, palettes, texture, post and shadow families.
claims.subject: style-techniques

claims.normalized_claim: Matcap lookup and subsurface wrap are research-only concepts and are intentionally absent from the UI technique dropdown.
claims.subject: research-only-style

claims.normalized_claim: Crest is treated as an architecture donor for separating material and geometry data from style interpretation, not as code to transplant.
claims.subject: Crest

claims.normalized_claim: Shadertoy, GodotShaders and gist snippets with unclear licensing are treated as concepts only rather than code sources.
claims.subject: snippet-sources

claims.normalized_claim: The stylized rendering plan composes background, hall textures, geometry effects, material shading, surface detail, effects, actors, atmosphere and post-processing as ordered layers.
claims.subject: stylized-rendering

claims.normalized_claim: Every stylized layer is intended to be optional and toggleable, with all stylization disabled by default.
claims.subject: stylized-rendering

claims.normalized_claim: StylizedSurfaceShader is proposed to combine quantized lighting with depth-and-normal contour extraction for a comic appearance.
claims.subject: StylizedSurfaceShader

claims.normalized_claim: HybridLineRenderer combines stable surface-space structural lines with supplemental screen-space depth and normal edges.
claims.subject: HybridLineRenderer

claims.normalized_claim: HatchingOperator is proposed to vary hatch density with shadow intensity, curvature and camera angle.
claims.subject: HatchingOperator

claims.normalized_claim: The stylized pipeline must not fork the shader source or change analyze material classification.
claims.subject: stylized-rendering

claims.normalized_claim: The document budgets the maximum combined stylized cost at roughly fifteen percent additional fillrate with the stylized features off in GOLD.
claims.subject: performance

extraction.notes: Motion research claims extracted without verification.

claims.normalized_claim: SHADED currently consumes SWIFT through sprite-sheet actors and manifests, while the motion-generation pipeline is not integrated.
claims.subject: SWIFT

claims.normalized_claim: The current SWIFT export is described as sprite sheet, manifest and optional depth data without exported joint trajectories.
claims.subject: SWIFT

claims.normalized_claim: The proposed manifest extension adds optional joints, per-frame positions, quaternion rotations and contact flags.
claims.subject: motion-manifest

claims.normalized_claim: Motion data is proposed to feed actor animation, SpatialKernel observations and world-law reactions such as footprints.
claims.subject: motion

claims.normalized_claim: The proposed motion chain is BodyParser to MotionSmoother to PositionToRotation to ContactDetector with optional partwise planning and interpolation.
claims.subject: motion-operators

claims.normalized_claim: The document recommends SWIFT exporting known rig trajectories directly instead of recovering joints from rendered pixel-art sprites with a vision model.
claims.subject: BodyParser

claims.normalized_claim: Motion data is optional and actors without it retain frame-based animation as the fallback behavior.
claims.subject: motion

claims.normalized_claim: The donor-map audit reports six spatial runtime modules had syntax defects and were repaired to pass node syntax checks.
claims.subject: spatial-runtime

claims.normalized_claim: The repaired modules are described as a largely orphaned subtree not reached by the live application.
claims.subject: spatial-runtime

claims.normalized_claim: SpatialSystemIntegrator contains simulated and flat depth fallback generators that must be explicit rather than presented as successful inference.
claims.subject: fallback-depth

claims.normalized_claim: spatial-reconstruction uses image-grid connected-component adjacency and is proposed to move to geometry-aware 3D neighbourhoods.
claims.subject: spatial-reconstruction

claims.normalized_claim: SparseVoxelWorld is described as a flat keyed map without chunks, dirty tracking, multi-resolution storage or confidence-weighted evidence fusion.
claims.subject: SparseVoxelWorld

claims.normalized_claim: The sparse-world disposition is to generalize toward a chunked SparseField while preserving canonical voxel state and provenance enums.
claims.subject: SparseField

claims.normalized_claim: Surface-world simulation is described as mixing authoritative state, solver behavior and visual effects and is proposed to split those concerns.
claims.subject: world-simulation

claims.normalized_claim: Navigation is described as Dijkstra-based without clearance, slope, portals, obstacle inflation or dirty-region path invalidation and is proposed to gain those capabilities.
claims.subject: navigation

claims.normalized_claim: Photo-first orchestration is proposed to become a recipe that emits GeometryObservation instead of remaining the architectural center of the kernel.
claims.subject: PhotoFirstRecipe

claims.normalized_claim: Depth-to-mesh and patch-registration logic are proposed to be retained and generalized behind the universal observation and SpatialMemory contracts.
claims.subject: geometry-pipeline

claims.normalized_claim: ReverseViewfinder is proposed to remain as a valuable manual-camera recipe rather than define the spatial core.
claims.subject: ReverseViewfinder
